items.title: Remote storage: background metadata sync and entry TTL
items.body:
## Summary

Depends on #8513 — please review only the 2 new commits on top of that PR.

- **Built-in background metadata sync**: New `-remoteMetaSyncInterval` flag (default 0 = disabled) starts a background goroutine that periodically traverses all remote mounts and upserts new or changed entries into the local store. Replaces the need for external `remote.meta.sync` cron jobs.
- **Remote entry TTL and revalidation**: New `-remoteEntryTTL` flag. When a stale entry is accessed via `FindEntry`, the filer re-stats the remote object: if unchanged, the sync timestamp is refreshed; if changed, chunks are cleared forcing re-fetch; if deleted, the local entry is removed. On remote errors, the stale entry is served for availability (stale-while-error).

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `-remoteMetaSyncInterval=30s` picks up new remote entries periodically
- [ ] Verify `-remoteEntryTTL=60s` revalidates stale entries on access
- [ ] Verify stale entries are served when remote is unreachable
- [ ] Verify changed remote files trigger chunk re-fetch
- [ ] Unit tests included for both features

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Remote metadata synchronization with configurable sync interval to keep local state updated.
  * Remote entry TTL with automatic revalidation and stale/removed detection.
  * Merging of remote directory listings into local directory views.
  * Two new CLI flags: --remoteMetaSyncInterval and --remoteEntryTTL to control remote behavior.

  * S3 TTL header/flag support, bucket-wide TTL update operation, and new APIs for checking/removing empty directories.

  * Preserve/propagate S3 TTL across uploads and multipart completes, disable native TTL deletion for S3-marked objects, batched expired-entry cleanup to avoid DB deadlocks, and safer bounded empty-directory removal during deletes.

  * Added lifecycle expiration tests and CI updates to run them.
